fullData.title: Adding Decimals on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Elementary Mathematics

problem.statement: Leo walks $0.6$ kilometers to the park, and then walks another $0.2$ kilometers to the ice cream shop. Use the number line below to find the total distance Leo walks by adding $0.6$ and $0.2$. What is the total distance?

fullData.solutionStrategy: Locate the first distance on the number line and jump forward by tenths to find the sum.

steps.title: Plot initial distance on number line

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into tenths, showing six jumps from 0 to 0.6.

annotations.steps: I start at 0 on the number line and jump forward six tenths to reach 0.6.
annotations.strategy: I notice that using a number line helps me see decimals as distances.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects whole number counting to decimal fractions on a continuous scale.
annotations.narrative: Locate the point labeled Start at $0$ and move along the number line to Park at tick mark $0.6$.

challenge.prompt: Starting at $0$, how many one-tenth ($0.1$) jumps forward does Leo need to make to reach the park at $0.6$?
challenge.rationale: Leo needs 6 jumps of 0.1 to reach 0.6, because each jump represents one tenth and we count the intervals rather than the starting tick mark.

steps.title: Jump forward to find total distance

content.altText: A number line from 0.0 to 1.0 divided into tenths, showing a jump of 0.2 forward from 0.6 to land at 0.8.

annotations.steps: I start at 0.6 on the number line and jump forward by 0.2 to land at 0.8.
annotations.strategy: I notice that adding decimals is just like jumping forward by tenths on a number line.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition to the same forward movement we use for whole number addition.
annotations.narrative: From $0.6$, jump forward $0.2$ (two tenths) along the number line to reach Ice Cream Shop at tick mark $0.8$. Since $0.6 + 0.2 = 0.8$, the total distance Leo walks is $0.8$ kilometers.

solverDebug.body:
Locate the point labeled Start at $0$ and move along the number line to Park at tick mark $0.6$.
---
From $0.6$, jump forward $0.2$ (two tenths) along the number line to reach Ice Cream Shop at tick mark $0.8$. Since $0.6 + 0.2 = 0.8$, the total distance Leo walks is $0.8$ kilometers.

specs.title: Plot initial distance on number line
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Visualize the first distance of 0.6 kilometers as an interval starting from 0 on a tenths number line.
specs.seedNotes: Draw a number line partitioned into tenths from 0 to 1, highlighting the move from Start at 0 to Park at 0.6.

specs.title: Jump forward to find total distance
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Model decimal addition as moving forward by tenths on the number line to find the final position.
specs.seedNotes: Illustrate a forward jump of +0.2 from 0.6 to arrive at 0.8 labeled Ice Cream Shop, showing 0.6 + 0.2 = 0.8 km.
